inputs.root_cause: A fresh contract_reconciler run (this session, after completing the ora render-engine slice) confirmed nrrd at 9/65 unresolved obligations. Two of them (SAL-NRRD-OBL-E4B3D1A206784660, SAL-NRRD-OBL-FEF73EC95DF631C3), both capability_id NRRD-ARRAY-001, share the same missing_behavior: no dtype/stride object, element API, slicing, permutation, flip, crop, metadata propagation, or view/copy contract exists anywhere in the package. NrrdDocument.array/.to_array() are a flat/nested Python list with no shape/strides/dtype object and no operations -- confirmed by a full repository read (production package structure, existing test coverage, dependency state) before writing any code.
inputs.obligation_targeted: SAL-NRRD-OBL-E4B3D1A206784660 and SAL-NRRD-OBL-FEF73EC95DF631C3 (both NRRD-ARRAY-001) together -- the two obligations are near-duplicates of each other (near-identical rule_text) and are closed by the same capability, not sequentially.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: Built format_factory.nrrd.array_view (module model/array_view.py): NrrdDtype (reusing codec/payload.py's existing dtype_info()/is_block_type()/parse_block_size(), not duplicating), AxisMetadata (kind/label/unit/spacing/axis-min-max/center/thickness/space-direction, one per axis), and NrrdArrayView (shape/strides/dtype, element access via __getitem__, zero-copy slicing/transpose/permute/flip/crop, explicit .copy()). No numpy dependency added -- the package's adapters/ directory already exists empty specifically for 'optional NRRD ecosystem adapters', signalling numpy (if ever added) belongs there as an additive layer, not a hard dependency; this implementation stays consistent with format-factory-core's and format-factory-ora's own zero-dependency, bounded-reader design. Per-axis metadata follows every operation: transpose reorders axis metadata (space_origin itself is axis-order-independent, unaffected); flip swaps axis_min/axis_max, negates space_direction, and shifts space_origin by (size-1)*old_direction to keep the view's own first element pinned at its pre-flip world-space position; slice/crop shift axis_min/axis_max by start*spacing when spacing is known, else clear them (None) rather than carry a stale bound forward. A 'range' kind axis (SAL-NRRD-00022, KIND_REQUIRED_SIZE not None -- e.g. a 3-color channel axis) refuses a slice/crop that would change its own element count, since that would change what the sample means, not resample it. Grounded directly against SAL-NRRD-00010/00011/00012/00015/00016/00019/00022 (none of which the raw obligation register cites via authority_fact_ids -- both target obligations show authority_fact_ids: [] -- so this session read the pinned SAL facts directly to ground the implementation rather than working from the obligation record's own citations alone).
